expectations.text: Identifies Q1 as double-barreled (combines speed and friendliness) and splits it into two items
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly labels Q1 'Defect: Double-barreled' and provides two rewritten items: Q1a on speed and Q1b on friendliness, each with a fully-labeled 5-point scale.

expectations.text: Flags Q2 as leading/loaded ('Don't you agree') and rewrites it with both poles offered
expectations.evidence: Response labels 'Leading wording' as one of two defects on Q2 and rewrites it: 'How would you rate the fairness of our pricing? (1 = Very unfair … 5 = Very fair)' — both poles present.

expectations.text: Notes that the agree/disagree format in Q2 is prone to acquiescence and/or suggests an item-specific alternative
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly names 'acquiescence' as the second defect on Q2, explaining it is stronger 'among lower-education respondents, distracted, or in high-deference social contexts,' and recommends an item-specific alternative.

expectations.text: Recommends replacing 'select all that apply' in Q3 with a forced-choice yes/no per option
expectations.evidence: Response recommends: 'Fix: forced-choice yes/no for each option' and provides a rewritten Q3 with 'Yes / No' per channel, citing Smyth et al. (2006) on satisficing.

expectations.text: Identifies the income question as sensitive and recommends a social-desirability mitigation (self-administered mode, ranges, confidentiality, and/or placing it late)
expectations.evidence: Response identifies 'social-desirability-risk' on Q4, notes the interviewer-administered phone mode worsens it, recommends banded income ranges with a 'Prefer not to say' option, and advises moving it to a self-administered web mode if possible.

expectations.text: Advises against numeric-only scales and recommends verbal labels on the points
expectations.evidence: Instrument-level section states 'Don't do this' for bare numbers and prescribes 'Label every point with words,' providing a fully-labeled example: '1 = Very dissatisfied … 5 = Very satisfied.'

expectations.text: Provides a concrete rewrite for at least three of the four questions, not just abstract critique
expectations.evidence: Concrete rewrites are provided for Q1 (two items with labeled scales), Q2 (item-specific rating rewrite), Q3 (forced-choice yes/no grid), and Q4 (banded income options) — all four questions receive rewrites.

claims.claim: Smyth et al. (2006) showed that check-all-that-apply questions systematically undercount endorsements due to satisficing
claims.evidence: This is a real and well-known finding; the citation is accurate.

claims.claim: Wording alone can shift responses by 20 percentage points or more on questions like Q2
claims.evidence: This magnitude of leading-question effect is consistent with the survey methods literature.

eval_feedback.overall: No suggestions — assertions are well-targeted and discriminating. The 7 assertions cover all major defects and correctly require concrete rewrites.
